content: Yaws is a tropical infectious disease that primarily affects the skin, bones, and joints. It is caused by a spiral-shaped bacterium known as Treponema pallidum subspecies pertenue. This bacterium is closely related to the one responsible for syphilis (Treponema pallidum), but unlike syphilis, yaws is not transmitted through sexual contact. Other diseases caused by related bacteria include bejel (Treponema endemicum), pinta (Treponema carateum), and Lyme disease (Borrelia burgdorferi). To diagnose yaws, a sample from a skin lesion is examined using a specialized technique called darkfield microscopy. This method allows for the visualization of the spiral-shaped bacteria. There is no specific blood test available for yaws. However, blood tests for syphilis often yield positive results in individuals with yaws due to the close relationship between the bacteria that cause these two diseases. The treatment for yaws typically involves a single dose of a specific type of penicillin. In cases where the disease has progressed to a later stage, three weekly doses of penicillin are administered. Recurrence of the disease after treatment is uncommon. It is important to examine and treat all individuals living in the same household as the infected person, as they may also be infected.
